routes.name: Entry Fee (visa-free entry)
routes.summary: Suriname replaced its visa with an online Entry Fee for most travelers. You pay online before the trip and show the voucher at airline check-in.

other: Most nationalities do not need a visa. 21 countries have needed a visa again since 2023, and Cuba, Venezuela and the Dominican Republic need a tourist card. The official pages read did not list the countries or the fee amount, so check the official list.
Proof of at least USD 25 per day or other sufficient means.

sources.label: Suriname government: visa and tourist card explainer

routes.name: Visa and Tourist Card (e-visa)
routes.summary: 21 countries must get a visa again since 2023. Cuba, Venezuela and the Dominican Republic also need a tourist card. Apply online only.

other: The country list was not shown on the official pages read. Check the embassy list of visa-required countries before you apply.

steps: Apply on the official e-visa site (suriname.vfsevisa.com) or the ministry e-visa app
Show the approval and voucher at airline check-in

sources.label: Suriname government: visa and tourist card explainer

routes.name: Residence Permit
routes.summary: A residence permit for up to 2 years that can be extended. Fees and full requirements were not on the official guide, so confirm with the Migration Department.

other: Fees and documents not confirmed. Contact Migratie@mofa.gov.sr.

routes.name: Work Permit
routes.summary: Your employer requests the work permit. It is valid for 1 year. You need legal stay and must pass the Basic Language Knowledge and Society Test.

other: Exempt: spouses of Surinamese nationals, people of Surinamese origin, PSA card holders, refugees and CARICOM skilled nationals.

routes.name: Co-Permanent Residence (family)
routes.summary: For spouses of permanent residents or Surinamese nationals. Minor children of legal residents get a Declaration of Residency.

other: Applicant must also hold a residence permit.
Spouse must have permanent residence or Surinamese nationality.

routes.name: Refugee and Asylum Residence Permit
routes.summary: Holders of a UNHCR certificate can get a residence permit for up to 1 year.

routes.name: Permanent Residence
routes.summary: Other immigrants can apply after holding a residence permit for 5 years. People of Surinamese origin have a separate indefinite-stay route.

other: 5 years on a residence permit for most applicants.

routes.name: Naturalization (Surinamese citizenship)
routes.summary: Apply to the Ministry of Justice and Police. Most immigrants need a residence permit for at least 5 years. People of Surinamese origin need 1 year.

other: Legal stay required, except for stateless people.
Marriage route: married to a Surinamese national for at least 2 years and a residence permit for at least 2 years.
Dual citizenship rules were not confirmed.

citizenship.note: Marriage route needs 2 years of marriage and 2 years on a residence permit.
